extraction.title: COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHIC STUDY OF THE COMMON COLD
key_findings: The common cold is associated with frequent and variable anatomical abnormalities in the upper airways, including occlusion of the ethmoid infundibulum and various sinus cavities.
Functional impairments such as abnormal nasal-airway resistance (94%) and delayed mucosal transport (61%) are highly prevalent during a cold.
Most anatomical and functional abnormalities observed during a cold resolve or significantly improve within two weeks, even without antibiotic treatment, indicating their reversible nature.
The study redefines the common cold as a viral rhinosinusitis, emphasizing the direct or indirect viral causation of sinus abnormalities.
The findings demonstrate a broader anatomical involvement of the upper airway in common colds than previously recognized, enhancing the understanding of its pathogenesis.
extraction.conclusion: The common cold is associated with frequent and variable anatomical involvement of the upper airways, including occlusion and abnormalities in the sinus cavities.
